rows.stem:
The main observations while performing the experiment of burning magnesium ribbon in air are :

(i) Magnesium ribbon burns with a dazzling white flame.

(ii) A white powder is formed.

(iii) Magnesium ribbon vapourises.

(iv) Aqueous solution of the white powder turns blue litmus to red.
rows.solution:
Magnesium burns with a dazzling white flame and forms a white powder, magnesium oxide. Magnesium does not vaporise, and magnesium oxide dissolves to give a basic solution, which turns red litmus blue (not blue litmus red). So only (i) and (ii) are correct.

This is option (C) (i) and (ii).

rows.stem: A metal, M, displaces iron from aqueous solution of ferrous sulphate but fails to do so in case of aqueous solution of aluminium sulphate. The metal M is
rows.solution:
M displaces iron, so it is more reactive than iron; it cannot displace aluminium, so it is less reactive than aluminium. Zinc lies between aluminium and iron in the reactivity series. (Magnesium would displace aluminium too, while copper and lead cannot displace iron.)

This is option (D) Zinc.

rows.stem: A common feature observed in the crystals of washing soda, copper sulphate, gypsum and ferrous sulphate is that all

options.label: C
options.text: have fixed number of molecules of water of crystallisation in one formula unit of these salts.

rows.solution:
Washing soda (\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)), copper sulphate (\(\mathrm{CuSO_4 \cdot 5H_2O}\)), gypsum (\(\mathrm{CaSO_4 \cdot 2H_2O}\)) and ferrous sulphate (\(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\)) each contain a fixed number of water molecules in one formula unit.

This is option (C) have fixed number of molecules of water of crystallisation in one formula unit of these salts.

rows.stem:
A metal, ‘X’, on treatment with sodium hydroxide liberates a gas ‘G’. It also liberates the same gas, ‘G’ on treatment with dilute sulphuric acid.

Based on above information, ‘X’ and ‘G’ respectively are
rows.solution:
Zinc reacts with sodium hydroxide to give sodium zincate and hydrogen, and with dilute sulphuric acid to give zinc sulphate and hydrogen:

\(\mathrm{Zn + 2NaOH \rightarrow Na_2ZnO_2 + H_2}\) and \(\mathrm{Zn + H_2SO_4 \rightarrow ZnSO_4 + H_2}\).

Copper reacts with neither. This is option (C) Zinc and Hydrogen.

rows.stem:
The values of **a**, **b**, **c** and **d** in the following balanced chemical equation are respectively :

\(\mathbf{a}\,\mathrm{Pb(NO_3)_2} \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} \mathbf{b}\,\mathrm{PbO} + \mathbf{c}\,\mathrm{NO_2} + \mathbf{d}\,\mathrm{O_2}\)
rows.solution:
\(\mathrm{2Pb(NO_3)_2 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} 2PbO + 4NO_2 + O_2}\)

Check: Pb 2 = 2; N 4 = 4; O 12 on the left, and \(2 + 8 + 2 = 12\) on the right.

So a, b, c, d are 2, 2, 4, 1, which is option (D) 2, 2, 4, 1.

rows.stem: During electrolytic refining of copper, the anode, the cathode and the electrolyte used respectively are

options.label: A
options.text: Impure copper, pure copper, acidified copper sulphate solution

options.label: B
options.text: Pure copper, impure copper, sulphuric acid

options.label: C
options.text: Pure copper, impure copper, acidified copper sulphate solution

options.label: D
options.text: Impure copper, pure copper, distilled water

rows.solution:
In electrolytic refining the impure metal is the anode, a thin strip of pure metal is the cathode, and a solution of a salt of the metal is the electrolyte. For copper this is acidified copper sulphate solution.

This is option (A) Impure copper, pure copper, acidified copper sulphate solution.

rows.stem: If we make carbon skeleton with four carbon atoms, the two different possible skeletons will be

options.label: A
options.text: Diagram (A) as printed - a three-carbon chain with a fourth carbon drawn below its last carbon; and a straight four-carbon chain; see the attached figure.

options.label: B
options.text: Diagram (B) as printed - a straight four-carbon chain; and a carbon bonded to a second carbon which carries two more carbons drawn diagonally up and down; see the attached figure.

options.label: C
options.text: Diagram (C) as printed - a straight four-carbon chain; and a two-carbon chain whose second carbon has two more carbons drawn vertically below it; see the attached figure.

options.label: D
options.text: Diagram (D) as printed - a straight four-carbon chain; and a two-carbon chain with one more carbon drawn below each of its carbons; see the attached figure.

rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - all four options are drawn carbon skeletons (a pair per option); the options ARE the figure. The placeholders below describe each drawing's layout without naming the skeletons. Page idx 6.
rows.solution:
Four carbon atoms can be joined in only two ways: a straight chain of four (C–C–C–C), and a chain of three with the fourth carbon attached to the middle carbon (a branched chain). The pair drawn in option (B) shows exactly these two: the straight chain, and a carbon joined to a central carbon that carries two more carbons, which is the branched skeleton.

In each of the other options the "second" skeleton is only the straight chain drawn bent, since its longest chain still has four carbons in a row.

This is option (B).

rows.stem:
Listed below are the steps of nutrition in Amoeba. Select the correct sequence of these steps :

(i) Diffusion of simple nutrients into cytoplasm

(ii) Food vacuole formation

(iii) Formation of finger like temporary extensions of cell surface

(iv) Complex substances broken to simpler ones

(v) Undigested material thrown out of the cell surface
rows.solution:
Amoeba first pushes out finger-like extensions (pseudopodia) around the food, which fuse to form a food vacuole. Inside the vacuole the complex food is broken down to simpler substances, which then diffuse into the cytoplasm. The undigested material is thrown out through the cell surface.

The order is (iii), (ii), (iv), (i), (v), which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Human Brain and Protection of Nervous Tissue
rows.stem: Which among the following is not a neural action controlled by the part of human brain labelled ‘X’ in the figure above ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - a drawn section of the human brain with an arrow labelled ‘X’ pointing at one part; which part X marks exists only in the drawing (withheld here, since naming it narrows the answer). Page idx 8.
rows.solution:
X marks the medulla in the hind-brain. The medulla controls involuntary actions such as salivation, vomiting and blood pressure. Hunger is controlled by the hypothalamus in the fore-brain.

So the action not controlled by X is option (B) Hunger.

rows.stem: The modes of reproduction in *Spirogyra* and *Planaria* respectively are
rows.solution:
*Spirogyra* breaks into pieces that grow into new individuals (fragmentation). *Planaria* can be cut into pieces, each of which regrows into a complete organism (regeneration).

This is option (C) Fragmentation and regeneration.

rows.stem: The plant hormones promoting rapid cell division in seeds and wilting of leaves respectively are
rows.solution:
Cytokinins promote cell division and are found where cells divide rapidly, as in seeds and fruits. Abscisic acid inhibits growth and causes wilting of leaves.

This is option (B) Cytokinins and Abscisic acid.

rows.stem: In aerobic respiration, the steps are : breakdown of glucose to pyruvate and its further conversion to carbon dioxide. Both processes respectively occur in –
rows.solution:
Glucose is broken down to pyruvate in the cytoplasm. In the presence of oxygen, pyruvate is broken down further to carbon dioxide and water in the mitochondria.

This is option (D) Cytoplasm and Mitochondria.

rows.stem: In order to obtain large images of the teeth of patients, the dentist holds the concave mirror in such a manner that the teeth are positioned

options.label: B
options.text: between pole and focus of the mirror.

options.label: C
options.text: between focus and centre of curvature of the mirror.

options.label: D
options.text: at the centre of curvature of the mirror.

rows.solution:
A concave mirror gives an enlarged, erect, virtual image only when the object is between the pole and the focus. So the dentist holds it with the teeth in that region.

This is option (B) between pole and focus of the mirror.

rows.chapter: The Human Eye and the Colourful World
rows.subtopic: Defects of Vision and their Correction
rows.stem: The possible way to restore clear vision of those people whose eyeball has elongated is the use of suitable
rows.solution:
An elongated eyeball causes myopia (near-sightedness): the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens of suitable power corrects it.

This is option (B) concave lens.

rows.stem: The examples of natural and manmade (artificial) ecosystems are respectively
rows.solution:
Lakes are natural ecosystems; gardens are made and maintained by people, so they are artificial (man-made) ecosystems. (Ponds, lakes and forests are natural; crop fields are man-made.)

This is option (C) Lakes and gardens.

rows.stem: Human activities that are affecting the environment are :

options.label: B
options.text: excessive use of disposable cups and plates.

options.label: C
options.text: maximising the use of reusable utensils for eating food and drinking fluids.

options.label: D
options.text: segregating the wastes into biodegradable and non-biodegradable before disposal.

rows.solution:
Excessive use of disposable cups and plates adds to waste and harms the environment. The other three choices are good practices that protect it.

This is option (B) excessive use of disposable cups and plates.

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight.

**Reason (R) :** Decomposition of silver chloride into silver and chlorine takes place by sunlight.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consists of **two** statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Silver chloride turns grey in sunlight, so the Assertion is true. This happens because sunlight decomposes it into grey silver and chlorine gas:

\(\mathrm{2AgCl(s) \xrightarrow{\text{sunlight}} 2Ag(s) + Cl_2(g)}\)

The Reason is true and is the correct explanation, which is option (A).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The embryo gets nutrition from the mother’s blood with the help of a special tissue called placenta.

**Reason (R) :** Placenta is a disc which is embedded in the uterine wall.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consists of **two** statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The embryo gets its nutrition from the mother's blood through the placenta, so the Assertion is true. The placenta is a disc embedded in the uterine wall, so the Reason is also true. But the Reason only describes the placenta; it does not explain how the embryo gets nutrition (through the villi on the embryo's side, which give a large surface for glucose and oxygen to pass).

Both are true and the Reason is not the correct explanation, which is option (B).

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** The pattern of the magnetic field of a solenoid carrying a current is similar to that of a bar magnet.

**Reason (R) :** The pattern of the magnetic field around a current carrying conductor is independent of the shape of the conductor.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consists of **two** statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
The field lines of a current-carrying solenoid look like those of a bar magnet, with one end acting as a north pole and the other as a south pole. The Assertion is true.

The pattern of the field around a current-carrying conductor depends on its shape (straight wire, circular loop, solenoid), so the Reason is false.

The Assertion is true while the Reason is false, which is option (C).

rows.stem:
**Assertion (A) :** All organisms can make organic compounds like sugar and starch from inorganic substances using radiant energy of the sun.

**Reason (R) :** The organisms which can produce food by photosynthesis are called producers.
rows.context: Question Nos. 17 to 20 consists of **two** statements – Assertion (A) and Reason (R). Answer these questions selecting the appropriate option from (A), (B), (C) and (D) given below :

options.label: A
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: B
options.text: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of the Assertion (A).

options.label: C
options.text: Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.

options.label: D
options.text: Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.

rows.solution:
Only autotrophs (green plants and some bacteria) can make sugar and starch from inorganic substances using sunlight. Animals and other heterotrophs cannot, so the Assertion is false.

Organisms that make food by photosynthesis are called producers, so the Reason is true.

The Assertion is false while the Reason is true, which is option (D).

rows.stem:
A crystalline substance of green colour ‘X’ emits gases of characteristic odour when heated over a flame. It first loses water and changes colour. On further heating, it decomposes and produces a solid compound Y.

(a) Identify ‘X’ and ‘Y’.

(b) State the change in colour observed when ‘X’ is heated.
rows.solution:
(a) X is hydrated ferrous sulphate (green crystals), \(\mathrm{FeSO_4 \cdot 7H_2O}\). Y is ferric oxide, \(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\).

\(\mathrm{2FeSO_4 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Fe_2O_3 + SO_2 + SO_3}\)

(b) On heating, the green crystals lose their water of crystallisation and turn white; on stronger heating the white solid turns reddish brown (\(\mathrm{Fe_2O_3}\)).

rows.stem:
Give reasons :

(a) The male reproductive organ responsible for formation of germ cells is located outside the abdominal cavity.

(b) The roles of the glands, present along the path of the vas-deferens, are very significant.
rows.solution:
(a) The testes are located outside the abdominal cavity, in the scrotum, because sperm formation needs a temperature lower than the normal body temperature.

(b) The secretions of the glands along the path of the vas deferens (the seminal vesicles and the prostate gland) make the sperms move more easily in a fluid and provide them with nutrition.

rows.stem: How is lymph formed ? State its important function.
rows.solution:
Through the pores in the walls of the capillaries, some plasma, proteins and blood cells escape into the spaces between the cells of the tissues. This fluid is called tissue fluid or lymph.

Functions (any one): lymph carries digested and absorbed fat from the intestine; it drains excess fluid from the spaces between cells back into the blood.

rows.stem:
(a) Identify ‘X’ in the figure of human nephron shown below. What role does it play in the process of urine formation ?

(b) Why some substances are selectively reabsorbed from the initial filtrate of urine, as it flows along the tabular part of nephron ?
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (a) asks to identify ‘X’ on a drawn human nephron; the drawing shows the nephron with its blood vessels and one arrow labelled ‘X’, and which structure X marks exists only in the drawing (withheld here, since naming it is the answer). Page idx 14.
rows.solution:
(a) X is Bowman's capsule. It collects the filtrate from the blood filtered in the glomerulus.

(b) Some substances, such as glucose, amino acids, salts and a large amount of water, are selectively reabsorbed because they are useful to the body. How much is reabsorbed depends on how much excess water there is in the body and how much dissolved waste has to be removed.

rows.stem:
The values of absolute refractive indices of kerosene and water are 1.44 and 1.33 respectively. Compare the two media on the basis of their

(a) optical density

(b) mass density

(c) relative speed of propagation of light.

What do you infer on the basis of above comparisons ?
rows.solution:
| Kerosene (1.44) | Water (1.33) |
|---|---|
| (a) Higher optical density | Lower optical density |
| (b) Lower mass density | Higher mass density |
| (c) Lower speed of light | Higher speed of light |

Inference: kerosene is optically denser than water but has a lower mass density. An optically denser medium need not have a greater mass density.

rows.stem:
(A) State two applications of Joule’s heating in domestic electric circuit.

(B) Establish the relationship between the commercial unit of electric energy and the SI unit of electric energy.
rows.solution:
(A) Any two: the electric bulb (filament), the electric iron, the electric heater, the electric oven, the electric fuse.

(B) The commercial unit is the kilowatt hour:

\(1\) kWh \(= 1000\) W \(\times 3600\) s \(= 3{\cdot}6 \times 10^6\) W s \(= 3{\cdot}6 \times 10^6\) J.

rows.stem:
(A) State two applications of Joule’s heating in domestic electric circuit.

(B) Determine the total resistance of the parallel combination of three resistances of \(2\,\Omega\), \(4\,\Omega\) and \(6\,\Omega\).
rows.solution:
(A) Any two: the electric bulb (filament), the electric iron, the electric heater, the electric oven, the electric fuse.

(B) \(\dfrac{1}{R_p} = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{4} + \dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{6 + 3 + 2}{12} = \dfrac{11}{12}\), so \(R_p = \dfrac{12}{11}\,\Omega \approx 1{\cdot}09\,\Omega\).

rows.stem:
(a) Why are the organisms of first trophic level important in any food chain ?

(b) Justify the following statement :

‘The flow of energy in an ecosystem is unidirectional.’
rows.solution:
(a) The organisms of the first trophic level (the producers) capture solar energy and convert it into chemical energy in food, which they make available to the consumers. Without them no energy would enter the food chain.

(b) The energy captured by the autotrophs does not go back to the sun, and the energy passed to the herbivores does not come back to the autotrophs. As energy moves through the trophic levels it is no longer available to the previous level, so the flow is in one direction only.

rows.subtopic: Common Salt and Chemicals from It
rows.stem: Write chemical formula of washing soda. How is it obtained from baking soda ? List two uses of washing soda.
rows.solution:
Washing soda is \(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\).

Heating baking soda gives sodium carbonate, and recrystallising sodium carbonate from water gives washing soda:

\(\mathrm{2NaHCO_3 \xrightarrow{\text{heat}} Na_2CO_3 + H_2O + CO_2}\)

\(\mathrm{Na_2CO_3 + 10H_2O \rightarrow Na_2CO_3 \cdot 10H_2O}\)

Uses (any two): in the glass, soap and paper industries; in the manufacture of borax; as a cleaning agent for domestic purposes; for removing permanent hardness of water.

rows.stem:
Observe the following diagram showing an experiment to determine the conditions under which a metal ‘M’ corrodes.

List your observations in each of the three cases A, B and C with reason, if the metal ‘M’ is generally protected against corrosion by the method of galvanisation.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - the contents of test tubes A, B and C are given only as labels on the drawing: three corked test tubes, A and B labelled 'Moist Air', 'Metal ‘M’' and 'Oil', C labelled 'Dry Air' and 'Metal ‘M’' with granules at its bottom. How far the metal sits in the oil in A and B is shown only in the drawing (not stated here). Page idx 18.
rows.solution:
Metal M, which is protected by galvanisation, is iron. Iron rusts only when both air and moisture are present.

A: the metal corrodes partly. The part outside the oil is exposed to moist air and rusts; the part inside the oil does not.

B: the metal does not corrode. It is covered by the oil and is not in contact with moist air.

C: the metal does not corrode, because the air in the tube is dry (the granules absorb moisture) and there is no water.

rows.stem:
(a) Show the formation of Aluminium Nitride (AlN) by the transfer of electrons. [ At. no. of Al = 13; At. no. of N = 7 ]

(b) “Ionic compounds are solids and are generally brittle and break into pieces when pressure is applied.” Give reason to justify the statement.
rows.solution:
(a) Al (2, 8, 3) has 3 valence electrons; N (2, 5) has 5. The aluminium atom loses its 3 valence electrons and the nitrogen atom gains them, so both reach a noble gas configuration:

\(\mathrm{Al \rightarrow Al^{3+} + 3e^-}\) and \(\mathrm{N + 3e^- \rightarrow N^{3-}}\)

The ions \(\mathrm{Al^{3+}}\) and \(\mathrm{N^{3-}}\) are held together as aluminium nitride, AlN. (In the dot diagram, the three electrons of Al are shown moving by arrows to N, which then carries a complete octet in brackets with a charge of \(3-\).)

(b) In ionic compounds the positive and negative ions are held by strong forces of attraction, so they are solids. When pressure is applied, the layers of ions shift so that ions of the same charge come face to face; they repel, and the crystal breaks into pieces. So ionic solids are brittle.

rows.stem:
(a) Write the name and one function of respiratory pigment found in human beings.

(b) Why do lungs always contain a residual volume of air ?

(c) Why is ATP known as energy currency of the living beings ?
rows.solution:
(a) The respiratory pigment in human beings is haemoglobin. It takes up oxygen in the lungs and carries it to the tissues that are deficient in oxygen.

(b) The lungs always keep some air (the residual volume) so that there is enough time for oxygen to be absorbed and carbon dioxide to be released.

(c) The energy released in respiration is used to make ATP, and ATP is then broken down to supply energy for the various activities in the cell. Because cells use it like money to "pay" for every energy-requiring process, ATP is called the energy currency of the cell.

rows.stem:
(a) Define fertilisation.

(b) What happens to Zygote, Ovule, Ovary and Stamens after fertilisation in a flowering plant ?
rows.solution:
(a) Fertilisation is the fusion of a male gamete with a female gamete to form a zygote.

(b) The zygote divides to form the embryo; the ovule develops into the seed; the ovary develops into the fruit; the stamens wither and fall off.

rows.subtopic: Lens Formula and Power of a Lens
rows.stem:
The power of a lens is \(-0.25\) D. Based on this information, find out

(a) The type of lens and its focal length.

(b) The eye defect for which it may be used as a corrective lens.

(c) The nature and size of the image formed by this lens when an object is placed between F and 2F from the optical centre of this lens.
rows.solution:
(a) \(f = \dfrac{1}{P} = \dfrac{1}{-0{\cdot}25} = -4\) m. The negative focal length shows it is a concave (diverging) lens.

(b) Myopia (near-sightedness).

(c) A concave lens always forms a virtual, erect and diminished image, between the optical centre and the focus, on the same side as the object.

rows.stem: The resistance of a wire of 0.01 cm radius is 7 ohms. If the resistivity of the material of the wire is \(44 \times 10^{-6}\) ohm meter, calculate the length of the wire.
rows.solution:
\(r = 0{\cdot}01\) cm \(= 10^{-4}\) m, so \(A = \pi r^2 = \dfrac{22}{7} \times 10^{-8}\) m\(^2\).

\(R = \rho\dfrac{l}{A}\) gives \(l = \dfrac{RA}{\rho} = \dfrac{7 \times \frac{22}{7} \times 10^{-8}}{44 \times 10^{-6}} = \dfrac{22 \times 10^{-8}}{44 \times 10^{-6}} = 0{\cdot}5 \times 10^{-2}\) m.

The wire is \(0{\cdot}5 \times 10^{-2}\) m, that is 0.5 cm, long.

rows.stem:
(a) “The third wire of earth connection is very important in domestic electric appliances.” Justify this statement.

(b) List two precautions to be taken to avoid the overloading of domestic electric circuits.
rows.solution:
(a) The earth wire is connected to the metal body of the appliance. If current leaks to the body, the earth wire gives it a low-resistance path to the ground and keeps the body at the potential of the earth, so the user does not get a severe electric shock.

(b) Any two: use a fuse of the proper rating in the circuit; do not connect too many appliances to a single socket; do not switch on many high-power appliances at the same time.

rows.stem:
(a) What is meant by the term homologous series of carbon compounds ? Write molecular formula of any two consecutive members of homologous series of ketones.

(b) Write chemical equation of the reactions of ethanoic acid with

(i) Sodium hydroxide and

(ii) Ethanol (in the presence of an acid); giving the name of the products in each case.

(c) Draw the structure of the molecule of benzene.
rows.solution:
(a) A homologous series is a series of carbon compounds in which the same functional group substitutes for hydrogen in a carbon chain; its members have the same general formula and similar chemical properties, and successive members differ by \(\mathrm{CH_2}\).

Two consecutive ketones: propanone, \(\mathrm{C_3H_6O}\) (\(\mathrm{CH_3COCH_3}\)), and butanone, \(\mathrm{C_4H_8O}\) (\(\mathrm{CH_3COC_2H_5}\)).

(b) (i) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + NaOH \rightarrow CH_3COONa + H_2O}\): the products are sodium ethanoate (sodium acetate) and water.

(ii) \(\mathrm{CH_3COOH + C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\): the product is the ester ethyl ethanoate, with water.

(c) Benzene, \(\mathrm{C_6H_6}\): six carbon atoms in a ring, with single and double bonds alternating around the ring, and one hydrogen attached to each carbon.

rows.stem:
(a) Write the molecular formula of ethyne and draw its electron dot structure.

(b) Write chemical equation to show the reaction of ethanol with

(i) Sodium metal

(ii) Ethanoic acid (in the presence of an acid)

(iii) Acidified potassium dichromate

Write the name of the product formed in each case.
rows.solution:
(a) Ethyne is \(\mathrm{C_2H_2}\). Its electron dot structure: the two carbon atoms share three pairs of electrons (a triple bond), and each carbon shares one pair with a hydrogen atom (\(\mathrm{H{-}C{\equiv}C{-}H}\) in structural form). Every carbon then has eight electrons and each hydrogen two.

(b) (i) \(\mathrm{2C_2H_5OH + 2Na \rightarrow 2C_2H_5ONa + H_2}\): sodium ethoxide (with hydrogen gas).

(ii) \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH + CH_3COOH \xrightarrow{\text{acid}} CH_3COOC_2H_5 + H_2O}\): ethyl ethanoate (an ester).

(iii) \(\mathrm{C_2H_5OH \xrightarrow{\text{acidified } K_2Cr_2O_7,\ \text{heat}} CH_3COOH}\): ethanoic acid.

rows.stem:
(a) Analyse the given situations and interpret the possible reason for each :

(i) Iodine deficiency in diet increases the possibility of a disease of swollen neck in a person.

(ii) Some people in population may have very short heights (dwarfs).

(iii) Thick facial hairs develop in boys at the age of 10-12 years.

(b) Explain two reasons which necessitate the need of chemical communication in multicellular organisms.
rows.solution:
(a) (i) Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to make thyroxine. Without enough iodine in the diet, the gland swells, causing goitre (a swollen neck).

(ii) Growth hormone from the pituitary gland controls growth. Its deficiency in childhood causes dwarfism.

(iii) At puberty, about 10 to 12 years of age, the testes secrete testosterone, which brings about changes such as facial hair in boys.

(b) Electrical impulses reach only the cells connected by nerve tissue, and cells cannot keep producing them continuously. Chemical signals (hormones) can reach all the cells of the body steadily and persistently, and they coordinate growth, development and responses to the environment.

rows.stem:
(a) Differentiate between voluntary and involuntary action.

(b) Define reflex action. With the help of a flow diagram, show the correct sequence of path of Nerve impulse from place of its origin.
rows.solution:
(a) Any two differences:

| Voluntary action | Involuntary action |
|---|---|

rows.stem:
(a) Observe the following diagram and compare (i) speed of light and (ii) optical densities of the three media A, B and C. Also give justification for your answer of any one of the two cases in terms of refractive indices of A, B and C.

(b) Redraw the path of a ray of light through the three media, if the ray of light starting from medium A falls on the medium B

(i) Obliquely and the optical density of medium B is made more than that of A and C.

(ii) The ray falls normally from medium A to medium B.
rows.figureNote: REQUIRED - (a) is answered from the drawn ray: a rectangular block labelled Medium B, with Medium A above it and Medium C below it, and one ray drawn from A through B into C. How the ray bends (or does not) at each face is shown only in the drawing and is withheld here, since it is the answer. Page idx 24.
rows.solution:
(a) In the figure the ray goes straight from A into B without bending, and bends away from the normal as it passes from B into C.

(i) The speed of light is the same in A and B, and greater in C.

(ii) The optical density of A and B is the same, and that of C is less.

Justification: the ray does not bend from A to B, so A and B have the same refractive index; it bends away from the normal from B to C, so C has a smaller refractive index. Refractive index is inversely proportional to the speed of light in a medium.

(b) (i) If B is made optically denser than A and C, a ray falling obliquely from A bends towards the normal as it enters B, and bends away from the normal as it passes from B into C. Draw the ray inside B closer to the normal than in A and C.

(ii) A ray falling normally from A on B passes straight through B and into C without bending.

rows.stem:
Analyse the following observation table showing variation of image distance (v) with object distance (u) in case of a convex lens and answer the questions that follow without doing any calculations :

| Observation Number | Object distance (u) in cm | Image distance (v) in cm |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | \(-15\) | \(-60\) |
| 2 | \(-25\) | \(+100\) |
| 3 | \(-30\) | \(+60\) |
| 4 | \(-40\) | \(+40\) |
| 5 | \(-60\) | \(+30\) |
| 6 | \(-100\) | \(+25\) |

(a) Determine the focal length of the lens. Give reason for your answer.

(b) Find magnification of the image formed in Observation No. 3.

(c) The numerical value of magnifications in cases of observation 1 and 2 is same. List two differences in the images formed in these two cases.
rows.solution:
(a) In observation 4, \(u = -40\) cm gives \(v = +40\) cm. For a convex lens the image is the same distance away on the other side only when the object is at 2F, so \(2f = 40\) cm and \(f = 20\) cm.

(b) \(m = \dfrac{v}{u} = \dfrac{+60}{-30} = -2\).

(c) Both magnifications have size 4 (\(\frac{-60}{-15} = +4\) and \(\frac{+100}{-25} = -4\)). In observation 1 the image is virtual and erect, on the same side as the object; in observation 2 it is real and inverted, on the other side of the lens.

rows.stem: An element A has atomic number 16, how will it attain its nearest noble gas configuration ?
rows.context: The combining capacity of various elements depends on the number of valence electrons. Also the reactivity of elements is explained as their tendency to attain a completely filled outer shell, that is, to attain a noble gas configuration. This may be either through gain of electrons or loss of electrons or sharing of electrons.
rows.solution: Element A (atomic number 16) is sulphur, with electronic configuration 2, 8, 6. It attains the nearest noble gas configuration (argon, 2, 8, 8) by gaining 2 electrons (forming \(\mathrm{S^{2-}}\)) or by sharing 2 electrons.

rows.stem: Write the number of (i) single and (ii) double covalent bonds in a molecule of butene \((\mathrm{C_4H_8})\).
rows.context: The combining capacity of various elements depends on the number of valence electrons. Also the reactivity of elements is explained as their tendency to attain a completely filled outer shell, that is, to attain a noble gas configuration. This may be either through gain of electrons or loss of electrons or sharing of electrons.

rows.stem: Explain the formation of a molecule of ammonia \((\mathrm{NH_3})\), using electron dot structure. (Atomic number of nitrogen is 7)
rows.context: The combining capacity of various elements depends on the number of valence electrons. Also the reactivity of elements is explained as their tendency to attain a completely filled outer shell, that is, to attain a noble gas configuration. This may be either through gain of electrons or loss of electrons or sharing of electrons.
rows.solution:
Nitrogen (2, 5) has 5 valence electrons and needs 3 more. Each hydrogen atom has 1 electron and needs 1 more.

The nitrogen atom shares one pair of electrons with each of three hydrogen atoms, forming three single covalent bonds. Nitrogen then has 8 electrons around it (three shared pairs and one lone pair), and each hydrogen has 2. In the dot diagram, N is drawn with its lone pair, and each N–H bond is a shared pair.

rows.stem: Why does carbon share its valence electrons with other atoms of carbon or with atoms of other elements ?
rows.context: The combining capacity of various elements depends on the number of valence electrons. Also the reactivity of elements is explained as their tendency to attain a completely filled outer shell, that is, to attain a noble gas configuration. This may be either through gain of electrons or loss of electrons or sharing of electrons.
rows.solution:
Carbon has 4 valence electrons. To reach a noble gas configuration it would have to gain 4 or lose 4 electrons, and neither is easy:

(i) gaining 4 electrons to form \(\mathrm{C^{4-}}\) would leave a nucleus of six protons holding ten electrons;

(ii) losing 4 electrons to form \(\mathrm{C^{4+}}\) would need a large amount of energy.

So carbon completes its octet by sharing its valence electrons with other carbon atoms or with atoms of other elements.

rows.stem: What are chromosomes ?
rows.context: In human beings, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes. Out of these 23 pairs of chromosomes (i.e. 46 chromosomes), 22 pairs of chromosomes are called autosomes and one pair of chromosomes. i.e. two chromosomes are called sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types – ‘X’ chromosomes and ‘Y’ chromosomes. The sex of a child (i.e. progeny), is decided at the time of fertilisation. In other words, at the time of zygote formation the sex chromosomes inherited from the parents of a child decide whether the new born will be a boy or a girl.
rows.solution: Chromosomes are thread-like structures in the nucleus that carry genes. They contain the information for the inheritance of features from parents to the next generation, in the form of DNA.

rows.stem: Why is the pair of sex chromosomes in human males called mismatched pair ?
rows.context: In human beings, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes. Out of these 23 pairs of chromosomes (i.e. 46 chromosomes), 22 pairs of chromosomes are called autosomes and one pair of chromosomes. i.e. two chromosomes are called sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types – ‘X’ chromosomes and ‘Y’ chromosomes. The sex of a child (i.e. progeny), is decided at the time of fertilisation. In other words, at the time of zygote formation the sex chromosomes inherited from the parents of a child decide whether the new born will be a boy or a girl.
rows.solution: In human males the sex chromosomes are X and Y. The X chromosome is of normal size but the Y chromosome is shorter, so the two do not match; they are called a mismatched pair. (Females have a matched pair, XX.)

rows.stem: Show with the help of a flow chart that the statistical probability of getting a boy or a girl is 50 : 50.
rows.context: In human beings, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes. Out of these 23 pairs of chromosomes (i.e. 46 chromosomes), 22 pairs of chromosomes are called autosomes and one pair of chromosomes. i.e. two chromosomes are called sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types – ‘X’ chromosomes and ‘Y’ chromosomes. The sex of a child (i.e. progeny), is decided at the time of fertilisation. In other words, at the time of zygote formation the sex chromosomes inherited from the parents of a child decide whether the new born will be a boy or a girl.
rows.solution:
Father (XY) produces two kinds of sperm, X and Y, in equal numbers. Mother (XX) produces only X eggs.

| Egg / Sperm | X | Y |
|---|---|---|
| X | XX (girl) | XY (boy) |
| X | XX (girl) | XY (boy) |

Half the zygotes are XX (girls) and half are XY (boys), so the probability of a boy or a girl is 50 : 50.

rows.stem: Mention two examples of animals where sex is not determined genetically like human beings. Describe in brief the method of sex determination in these animals.
rows.context: In human beings, there are 23 pairs of chromosomes. Out of these 23 pairs of chromosomes (i.e. 46 chromosomes), 22 pairs of chromosomes are called autosomes and one pair of chromosomes. i.e. two chromosomes are called sex chromosomes. The sex chromosomes are of two types – ‘X’ chromosomes and ‘Y’ chromosomes. The sex of a child (i.e. progeny), is decided at the time of fertilisation. In other words, at the time of zygote formation the sex chromosomes inherited from the parents of a child decide whether the new born will be a boy or a girl.
rows.solution:
1. In some reptiles, the temperature at which the fertilised eggs are kept decides whether the young will be male or female.

2. In snails, an individual can change its sex, which shows that sex is not decided genetically.

rows.stem: By convention, the field lines emerge from north pole and merge at south pole. Why ? Give reason.
rows.context: In order to obtain magnetic field lines around a bar magnet, a student performed an experiment using a magnetic compass and a bar magnet. The magnet was placed on a sheet of white paper fixed on a drawing board. Using magnetic needle he obtained on the paper a pattern of magnetic field lines (as shown below) around the bar magnet.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the passage shows the field-line pattern around a bar magnet (poles S and N, closed loops with arrows); no sub-part needs a quantity read off it. Page idx 28.
rows.solution: By convention, the direction of the magnetic field at a point is the direction in which the north pole of a compass needle placed there moves. A north pole is repelled by the magnet's north pole and attracted by its south pole, so outside the magnet the field lines go from the north pole to the south pole.

rows.stem: State the relationship between strength of the magnetic field and the degree of closeness of the field lines.
rows.context: In order to obtain magnetic field lines around a bar magnet, a student performed an experiment using a magnetic compass and a bar magnet. The magnet was placed on a sheet of white paper fixed on a drawing board. Using magnetic needle he obtained on the paper a pattern of magnetic field lines (as shown below) around the bar magnet.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the passage shows the field-line pattern around a bar magnet (poles S and N, closed loops with arrows); no sub-part needs a quantity read off it. Page idx 28.
rows.solution: The closer the field lines, the stronger the magnetic field: the degree of closeness of the lines shows the relative strength of the field.

rows.stem:
(i) No two field lines can ever intersect each other. Give reason.

(ii) The magnetic field in a given region is uniform. Draw a diagram to represent it.
rows.context: In order to obtain magnetic field lines around a bar magnet, a student performed an experiment using a magnetic compass and a bar magnet. The magnet was placed on a sheet of white paper fixed on a drawing board. Using magnetic needle he obtained on the paper a pattern of magnetic field lines (as shown below) around the bar magnet.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the passage shows the field-line pattern around a bar magnet (poles S and N, closed loops with arrows); no sub-part needs a quantity read off it. Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
(i) If two field lines crossed, the compass needle at the point of intersection would have to point in two directions at once, which is not possible.

(ii) A uniform field is drawn as equally spaced, parallel straight lines, all with arrows in the same direction. (The field inside a long solenoid is an example.)

rows.subtopic: Magnetic Field due to a Solenoid
rows.stem: Draw the pattern of the magnetic field lines through and around a current carrying solenoid. What does the pattern of field lines inside the solenoid represent ?
rows.context: In order to obtain magnetic field lines around a bar magnet, a student performed an experiment using a magnetic compass and a bar magnet. The magnet was placed on a sheet of white paper fixed on a drawing board. Using magnetic needle he obtained on the paper a pattern of magnetic field lines (as shown below) around the bar magnet.
rows.figureNote: ILLUSTRATIVE - the passage shows the field-line pattern around a bar magnet (poles S and N, closed loops with arrows); no sub-part needs a quantity read off it. Page idx 28.
rows.solution:
Draw a solenoid connected to a cell and a key. Inside it the field lines are parallel straight lines along its axis; outside they curve round from one end to the other, like those of a bar magnet, with one end acting as a north pole and the other as a south pole.

The parallel straight lines inside the solenoid show that the magnetic field there is uniform (the same at all points).
